title: Air Quality and Outdoor Activity Guidance for Schools
claims: Green (Good): a great day to be active outside.
Yellow (Moderate): a good day to be active outside; students who are unusually sensitive could have symptoms.

Orange (Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups): short activities such as recess and physical education are still OK; for longer activities such as athletic practice, take more breaks and do less intense activities, and watch for symptoms.
Red (Unhealthy): for all outdoor activities, take more breaks and do less intense activities; consider moving longer or more intense activities indoors or rescheduling them.
Purple (Very Unhealthy): move all activities indoors or reschedule them to another day.
There is less ozone in the morning; on days when ozone is expected to be unhealthy, plan outdoor activities in the morning.

Symptoms to watch for include coughing, wheezing, difficulty breathing and chest tightness; if symptoms occur, take a break, reduce intensity, stop, go indoors or use prescribed quick-relief medicine, and get medical help if they do not improve.
